key_insight: Megrez coordinates a general coding agent with library knowledge, live proof feedback, and integration checks to formalize textbook mathematics in Rocq over MK set theory.
engineering_relevance: The design addresses practical bottlenecks in growing formal libraries: finding relevant declarations, tracking proof states, and safely integrating verified results.
method: Rebuildable knowledge graph combines declarations, compiler references, and curated metadata for multilingual, dependency-aware retrieval.
Short bursts of 1–5 tactics use proof-state feedback, a goal-local branch ledger, and structured reflection at exponential intervals.
Statement-fidelity checks, axiom audits, and full builds gate acceptance, supported by multi-corpus providers and recoverable batch execution.
evidence_signal: Deployment and evaluation on a point-set topology corpus report effective cross-chapter formalization and scalable premise retrieval, without quantitative results in the abstract.
watch_item: Performance beyond the evaluated topology corpus remains unclear, and maintaining curated metadata may add implementation overhead.
paper_title: Megrez: A Knowledge-Guided Agent for Formal Mathematics over MK Set Theory
